title: Token throughput microprobe suite for core models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build and maintain a lightweight, production-oriented token-throughput microprobe ("microprobe") for Redwood core model serving. The microprobe will provide deterministic tokens/sec measurements, p95 latency tracking, and automated regression detection that can be run ad-hoc and in CI. It must be reproducible across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and be fast enough to run as a nightly CI job and on-demand canary checks. Focus is on realistic prompt mixes, KV cache warm/cold scenarios, and sample-level tracing for root-cause analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Microprobe produces stable tokens/sec and p95 metrics for configured model variants with less than 5% intra-run variance across 10 runs.
Nightly CI job executes the suite for the primary 3 core models and uploads time-series to the benchmarking dashboard.
Regression detector flags >5% tokens/sec drop or >10% p95 increase relative to baseline and opened a GitHub issue with perf artifact links.
Results include KV cache warm/cold breakdown, sequence-length bucketed tokens/sec, and per-run trace IDs for reproducing slow tails.
Test harness is configurable via YAML and supports running against hosted, dedicated, and private endpoints with the same CLI/SDK interface.
test_matrix: Models: rwd-base-13b, rwd-chat-7b, rwd-embed-2.7b (canary list expandable)
KV cache modes: cold start (no KV), warm (prefill with canonical prompts)
Network modes: local loopback (unit), intra-region (low latency), cross-region (simulated higher latency)
Workload shapes: steady stream, bursty microburst (spikes), stepped sustained load to establish steady-state tokens/sec
implementation_plan: Design harness API and YAML config schema (prompts, seed corpus, sequence buckets, cache-mode)
Implement runner CLI/SDK that emits tokens/sec and p95 with deterministic sampling and per-request tracing headers
Add KV prefill utility to reproduce warm cache conditions deterministically
Integrate with CI: nightly GitHub Actions job and optional pre-merge smoke step for runtime changes
Publish baseline runs for three core models (artifact upload to s3 + register baseline commit hashes)
Wire regression detector to create GitHub issues and Slack alerts when thresholds are crossed
Document runbook for investigating regressions including trace correlation and rollbacks
monitoring_and_alerting: Upload metrics to bench-dashboard (prometheus time-series push): tokens/sec, p95, p99, variance
Create Grafana dashboard with historical baseline bands and per-model heatmap
Regression detector generates a summarized report (CSV + link to raw traces) and posts to #perf-alerts
Add automated PR comment summarizing perf delta when a PR touches runtime or kernels
Retention: keep raw traces for 30 days, aggregated metrics for 90 days
